       5             : /** \file
       6             :  * \ingroup sequencer
       7             :  *
       8             :  * Cache open movie readers for reuse across rendered frames.
       9             :  * - Readers are keyed by source file path and decode settings, not by strip. So neighboring
      10             :  *   strips that use the same media can use the same reader.
      11             :  * - Each rendering thread (e.g. the main render and prefetch) keeps its own readers. Sharing one
      12             :  *   between concurrent renders could make each render re-seek (and re-decode) on every frame.
      13             :  * - A reader is reserved after use until the next top-level frame render, so multiple strips using
      14             :  *   the same media do not seek one reader back and forth within the same frame.
      15             :  * - From the available matching readers of the current thread, prefer the one closest to the
      16             :  *   requested source frame, with a penalty for readers that need to seek backwards.
      17             :  * - Frame-independent queries can reuse any free matching reader. Querying an initialized reader
      18             :  *   does not change its decode position. Such queries may temporarily grow the cache beyond its
      19             :  *   soft size limit; stale entries are removed when subsequent frames are rendered.
      20             :  * - Cache size uses #MovieReaderCache::max_entries as a soft limit. Readers above it are removed
      21             :  *   after they have not been used for #MovieReaderCache::stale_after_timestamps render timestamps.
      22             :  */
